Scope the release dry run's ref check to refs it can move (#290)

tools/release-dry-run.sh hashed every ref of the repository before its
run and in step 6, so a ref that another worktree moved during the run
failed it, although the dry run had moved nothing (TODO 279, seen on
the PR 284 gate). Step 6 now compares only the refs that the dry run
could itself move, read from the worktree that holds the script before
and after: the branch HEAD names, or that it is detached; the commit
HEAD resolves to; and every tag and note with its object name. It
prints both snapshots on a mismatch, so the failure names the ref that
differs. It then fails when any ref of any namespace contains the
dry-run commit, which the script records after its commit. A git error
in either check fails the run and is never read as an empty listing.

This narrows a release-integrity check on purpose and needs the
maintainer's acceptance. Step 6 newly catches a commit on a detached
HEAD, and a detach or an attach at the same commit, which the old hash
missed because git for-each-ref lists no HEAD. It no longer catches
the deletion of any ref outside tags and notes other than the
checked-out branch, such as another branch, a remote-tracking ref,
refs/stash or a refs/replace/ ref; a move or creation of such a ref at
a commit that does not contain the dry-run commit, or at an object
that peels to no commit, such as a tree or a blob; or such a deletion,
move or creation made by a commit hook. The script's header states
that residual. A write that another worktree makes during the run
still fails it when it is a tag or a note, the HEAD of the script's
worktree or its checked-out branch, or a ref put on the dry-run commit
or a descendant of it. TODO 279 does not record which ref moved on the
PR 284 gate, so whether this change would have avoided that failure
is unknown.

tools/test-release-dry-run-refs.py runs the script's own functions,
before line, dry-run commit line and step 6, extracted by content
anchors, in throwaway repositories in a temporary folder. It refuses a
script that defines one of those functions again, or assigns the
before or dry-run commit variable again, on any other line. It runs 27
ref cases, with concurrency modelled as sequenced writes from a second
worktree, each checking that exactly the refs it names change, 6 cases
on fail-closed reading and structure, and 3 that remove, repeat or add
again each extraction anchor, function and variable. Its first version
of 21 cases, run against the unchanged script, failed the concurrent
cases and passed the detached commit; against this change all 36 cases
pass. Each of 14 mutants that remove 1 stated rule failed at least 1
case of the previous 33-case suite, and each of 10 later mutants fails
at least 1 of the 36. The release dry run workflow and
tools/run_all_checks.sh run it before the dry run, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of
tools/run_all_checks.sh after a reading of the whole script. The
workflow header now counts 7 test suites.
